newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Three strong IPOs, Cymer a hit.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Three strong IPOs, Cymer a hit.

text.p: Investors snapped up shares of three IPOs on Tuesday, making their stocks some of the highest flying deals on the Nasdaq on a percent basis.
Cymer Corp led the deals. Its shares rose 42 percent after its initial public offering on Thursday, the highest rise on the Nasdaq Composite Index.

The San Diego company makes excimer lasers for deep ultraviolet photolithography systems, which make the very small images used in manufacturing advanced semiconductor chips. Its shares rose 3-7/8 to 13-3/8.
Cymer shares had priced at the high end of their estimated pricing range of $7.50 to $9.50. Morgan Stanley was the lead underwriter of the 3.34 million share offering.

Rental Services Corp which rents out pumps, generators, forklifts and other industrial equipment, rose 5-1/4 to 21-1/4, or 32 percent after its market debut. Smith Barney was the lead underwriter of the offering.
The Scottsdale, Arizona company offered 5.5 million shares, which priced at the high end of the estimated $14 to $16 a share range.
RMH Teleservices Inc, which provides outbound teleservices for insurance and financial services companies, also rose strongly after its market debut. Its shares rose 3-1/2, or 28 percent, to 16.

RMH sold a roughly 26 percent stake to the public in the 2.8 million share offering, according to a regulatory filing. Based in Bryn Mawr, Pa., it posted operating income of $2.0 million of revenues of $25.5 million in fiscal 1995.
All three deals had been forecast as hot issues by analysts.
Q.E.P. shares remained flat at 9 after their Wednesday market debut. They rose 1/2 yesterday from their IPO price of 8-1/2.
